newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-McIntosh shares jump on Merrill bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-McIntosh shares jump on Merrill bid.

text.p: Shares in listed stockbroker McIntosh Securities Ltd opened 13 cents higher at A$1.38 after reinstatement to trading following its announcement of an agreed takeover bid.
The brokerage firm said it had agreed to a A$1.40 per share takeover bid by U.S. financial services group Merrill Lynch and Co Inc, valuing the company at about A$117 million.
Brokers said the offer looked to be fully-priced with the McIntosh board agreement obviously a big boost to the deal.
"It is fully priced and looks to be a done deal at that price," said a Sydney broker.
Other players held similar views, saying the bid looked convincing, even given the difficulties in valuing a stockbroker's shares.
"It's hard to price a broker's stock but in relation to what they have been recently it seems to be a pretty full price," said a Perth-based dealer.
The offer represents a premium of about 48 percent on McIntosh's average closing price in the last 30 days. It also represents 11.1 times pre-tax profits and 1.3 times net assets.
By 12.30 p.m. (0130 GMT), McIntosh shares were 15 cents higher at A$1.40 on turnover of 54,160 shares.
